pages.api:
# API reference

> The reading, the report, the store vector, the export endpoints and the settings.

## Reading `video.frame-ref/<source>`

`video.frame-ref.v1`, class `reading`: `source_id`, `node_id`, `t_ns`, `seq`, `hash` (BLAKE3 of the JPEG, 64 lower-case hex), `width`, `height`, `pixel_format` (`mjpeg`), `ttl_ms`, and `blob` (a `blob.v1` handle to the JPEG in the node's blob store, when it was put there; its `hash` equals `hash`). The bytes are also in the cog's data directory as `frames/<hash>.jpg` for `ttl_ms`.

## Reading `telemetry/<source>`

`telemetry.v1`: `frames.total`, `frames.rate` (fps), `frames.refs`, `capture.errors`, `frame.width`, `frame.height`, `bus.connected`.

## stdout report (one per interval)

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `ok`, `no_source`, `simulate`, `replay` |
| `provenance` | string | `MEASURED`, `SYNTHETIC` or `REPLAY` |
| `source`, `device` | string | the source id; `v4l2:<node>`, `simulated`, `replay`, `none` |
| `frames`, `fps` | numbers | frames kept in the window and their rate |
| `width`, `height` | number/null | size of the last frame |
| `mean_frame_kb` | number | mean JPEG size |
| `frame_refs_published` | number | readings sent to the broker |
| `blobs_put` | number | frames put in the blob store |
| `capture_errors` | number | unreadable frames |
| `last_hash` | string/null | hash of the newest frame |
| `bus` | object | `connected`, `seq`, `error` |
| `error` | string | only with `no_source` |

## Store vector (id 31)

Eight floats; a source that is absent is **-1**.

| Slot | Name | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `fps` | frames per second |
| 1 | `width` | px |
| 2 | `height` | px |
| 3 | `mean_frame_kb` | KiB |
| 4 | `frames` | count in the window |
| 5 | `bus_connected` | 0 or 1 |
| 6 | `capture_errors` | count |
| 7 | `refs_published` | count |

## Export (`http://127.0.0.1:8065`, continuous mode)

`/status` latest report, `/raw` the latest frame handle, `/frame.jpg` the latest JPEG, `/history` the last 60 reports, `/guide` this guide, `/healthz`. Loopback only.

## Settings

`--interval`, `--fps`, `--width`, `--height`, `--ttl-ms`, `--no-blob`, `--source`, `--camera-name`, `--device`, `--frames-dir`, `--api-bind`, `--replay`, `--simulate`.
pages.device:
# The device

> Which video node is opened, and how to choose between two cameras.

The host hands the owner the video nodes it declared (`/dev/video*`) in the environment variable `WEFTOS_DEVICES`. A UVC camera shows two nodes: the video node and a metadata node. The cog picks the lowest node whose `/sys/class/video4linux/<node>/index` is `0`, which is the video node.

## Choosing between cameras

With several cameras (for example the board's own CSI cameras and a USB camera), set **Camera name** to part of the name in `/sys/class/video4linux/<node>/name` (matched without regard to case), such as `U20CAM`.

## What it asks the camera for

MJPEG at the width, height and frame rate in the settings (1280x720 at 2 fps by default). A camera that cannot do that combination makes the capture fail; the report says `no_source` with the pipeline's message. Try `v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video0 --list-formats-ext` for what it can do.

## By hand

`--device /dev/video0` opens a node you name, whether or not the host handed it. Use it for a bench run from a shell.

## Ownership

Only one cog owns the video nodes. Placing a second cog that declares `/dev/video*`, or whose arguments name a `/dev/video` node, is refused.
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Run it from a shell, then place it on the node.

## From a shell

```
cog-camera --once --device /dev/video0                  # a few frames, prints a report
cog-camera --device /dev/video0 --fps 5 --width 640 --height 480
```

With `WEFTOS_COGBUS` and `WEFTOS_COGBUS_TOKEN` set (the host sets them for a placed cog) the cog publishes one `video.frame-ref.v1` reading per frame. Without them it still captures, stores and reports; the report's `bus.connected` is false and `frame_refs_published` stays 0.

## Placed on a node

Place `camera` through the controller like any cog. Its `cog.toml` declares the device (`[[devices]] path = "/dev/video*"`) and the two outputs. The host refuses the placement if another cog owns a video node.

## Needs

- `gst-launch-1.0` with the `v4l2src` and `multifilesink` elements (GStreamer base and good plugins) on the board.
- Read and write access to the video node for the user the cog runs as (the `video` group on a stock image).
pages.start:
# Start here

> Make the board's camera available to every other cog, without any of them opening it.

`camera` is the one owner of the V4L2 device. It captures MJPEG frames and announces each as a `video.frame-ref.v1` reading on `video.frame-ref/<source>`: a BLAKE3 hash of the frame, its size, `mjpeg`, and how long the bytes are kept. A detector or a viewer cog reads the readings and fetches the bytes by hash.

## The short path

1. **See which cameras the board has.** `v4l2-ctl --list-devices`, or `ls /dev/video*`. → see **The device**
2. **Run it once.** `cog-camera --once --device /dev/video0` captures a few frames and prints a report. → see **Set up**
3. **Look at a frame.** Run it continuously and open `http://127.0.0.1:8065/frame.jpg` on the board.
4. **Install it as a placed cog.** The host hands it the video nodes and nothing else. → see **Set up**

You can test with no camera: `--once --simulate` announces frames with valid structure and no image, marked `SYNTHETIC`, and `--replay FILE.jpg` announces a real picture through the same path.

## How the signal flows

```diagram
flow
```

## Honest limits

- The pixels do not go in the reading. Each frame is also put in the node's blob store (WeftOS ADR-122 B5), and the reading carries its `blob.v1` handle in `blob`: a reader that receives the reading may fetch the JPEG or hand the handle to a service (a vision model) in a call. Without a broker, or with **No blob store** set, the reading has only the hash; the bytes are then reachable on this node's loopback, from the data directory or at `/frame.jpg` (the latest one).
- Frames are MJPEG as the camera makes them. Nothing is decoded here. H.264 on request is not implemented.
- A frame's bytes are deleted after `--ttl-ms` (10 s by default); a reading older than that points at nothing.
- On a node where every cog runs under one user id, the node refuses a second claim on the camera but cannot stop a cog from opening `/dev/video0` behind its back. The listing says `device_isolation: advisory`.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> What each failure looks like and what to do.

## `no_source`

The report's `error` says why.

| `error` starts with | Meaning | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| `no video node in WEFTOS_DEVICES` | the host handed no video node | place the cog through the controller, or pass `--device` |
| `no handed capture node matches` | the camera name matches none of the handed nodes | check `/sys/class/video4linux/*/name` and the **Camera name** setting |
| `gst-launch-1.0: ...` | GStreamer is missing | install the GStreamer tools and base and good plugins |
| `gst-launch-1.0 exit status: 1` | the pipeline failed | run the same pipeline by hand: `gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video0 num-buffers=2 ! image/jpeg,width=1280,height=720 ! fakesink` and read its message |
| `the camera delivered no frames in time` | the node is busy or not a capture node | another process holds the camera; check `fuser /dev/video0` |

## Frames per second is below the setting

The camera lowers its rate in low light (auto exposure) or the USB port is shared. Try a smaller size.

## `bus.connected` is false

`bus.error` holds the broker's refusal. `unauthorized` or `unknown_topic` means the cog was placed without its `[[outputs]]`; place the package again.

## A reading's hash is not on disk

The ttl passed. Raise **Frame lifetime** or fetch sooner.

# Sensor guide for camera (WeftOS ADR-104 sensor-guide format, schema 1).
# Pages are Markdown files next to this one (guide/<page>.md).

schema = 1
title = "A USB camera on a Linux board"
sensor = "V4L2 camera (UVC, MJPEG)"
cog = "camera"
cog_version = "0.1.0"
medical = false
pages = ["start", "device", "setup", "troubleshoot", "api"]

# Checklist step ids the companion app links to a page.
[links]
cog_installed = "setup"
cog_running = "setup"
device = "device"
frames = "troubleshoot"
no_source = "troubleshoot"

# Signal flow, left to right.
[[flow]]
name = "Camera"
detail = "UVC, MJPEG"

[[flow]]
name = "gst-launch-1.0"
detail = "v4l2src to multifilesink"

[[flow]]
name = "camera cog"
detail = "hash, size, keep for ttl"

[[flow]]
name = "Outputs"
